title: On-call cognitive load mitigation and dynamic priority curve for noisy SLO burn
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: During multi-region partial degradations and regional failovers we generate a flood of pages that overloads on-call engineers and leads to noisy escalations and longer mean time to mitigation. Existing thresholds treat all alerts as equal and do not account for SLO context, circuit-breaker state, or operator cognitive load.

Goal: Reduce unnecessary paging noise while preserving timely signals for real user impact. Introduce a dynamic priority curve that reclassifies alert severity based on SLO burn, regional redundancy state, circuit-breaker/load-shedding decisions, and correlated signal density. Provide an "operator cushion" period and automated transient resolution attempts before paging primary on-call. Couple this with runbook templates and automation steps that can be invoked automatically for known transient failures.

Non-goals: Replace PagerDuty/ops workflow entirely or remove pages for high-severity incidents that break user-facing SLOs. This ticket focuses on policy, signal correlation, and automation hooks; instrumentation and UI changes are separate child tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A policy engine exists that maps SLO burn + region redundancy + circuit-breaker state to a comms decision (notify, suppress, or reclassify to low).
Real traffic experiments show >=50% reduction in duplicated pages for region-cutover scenarios in staging without increasing time-to-first-ack for high-impact incidents.
Runbooks for the top 5 frequent page triggers are available in Console and can be executed via a single automated remediation action.
New dashboard panels show per-alert operator load score, page suppression rate, and SLO-linked missed-page incidents for the last 30 days.
design_notes: Priority curve: numeric score = w1*SLO_burn_rate + w2*region_redundancy_penalty + w3*alert_density - w4*automated_mitigation_success. We will start with weights {w1:0.6,w2:0.2,w3:0.15,w4:0.05} and tune based on incident replay.

Operator cushion: when score falls into 'soft' range (0.3-0.6) buffer for 90s to 180s and concurrently attempt non-intrusive automated mitigation (retry upstream connections, queue drain, restart transient worker). Only escalate if automated attempts fail or score rises.

Circuit-breaker integration: queries of CB state are used to suppress pages for degraded capacity patterns that are expected and already being shed. If CB toggles from closed->open quickly across many hosts, escalate immediately (indicates systemic regression).

Multi-region deduplication: tags alerts by customer-region and failover-tag. If same incident surfaces from secondary region after automated cutover planned by routing policy, count as continuation rather than new page. Use correlation window of 10 minutes by default.

Trade-offs: adds small delay to some pages (operator cushion). Risk of delayed response if mitigation automation does not cover novel failures. Mitigation: default thresholds conservative and roll out in monitor-only for 2 weeks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (monitor-only): Implement scoring pipeline and surface decisions in a 'would-page' dashboard for 2 weeks (staging + prod sampling).
Phase 1 (soft-mute): Enable operator cushion and automated mitigation for low-density incidents in prod for non-critical namespaces (5% traffic). Observe metrics for 1 sprint.
Phase 2 (wider rollout): Expand to 25% then 100% after tuning weights and automated remediation success rate > 60% for top 10 triggers.
Fallback: feature flag to immediately open pages and a kill-switch to revert to prior behavior within PagerDuty.
dashboards: SLO burn vs page rate: heatmap of SLO burn buckets and mean pages/minute
Operator load score timeline: per-oncall aggregated score and paging events
Correlation efficacy: fraction of duplicate pages merged by correlation engine
Automated mitigation success: success/failure counts and time-to-success distribution
runbook_snippets: Runbook: 'regional-egress-failure' - steps: 1) check CB state for egress service, 2) attempt graceful failover via routing API (1 click), 3) check kv-cache warm status, 4) escalate if latency > 2x for 10m.
Runbook: 'queue-thrashing' - steps: 1) pause ingestion worker group via orchestrator, 2) drain and backpressure suppliers, 3) apply temporary scale-up policy, 4) resume with telemetry watch
Example: Provide single-button 'Try Automated Mitigation' in Console that runs pre-approved remediation playbook and posts status back to the alert thread.
automation_tasks: Implement scoring pipeline: new service 'alert-orchestrator' that consumes alert stream, queries SLO service and CB state, evaluates priority curve, and emits paging decision. (ENG-600112 is infra for streaming hooks).
Create templated remediation scripts for top 5 triggers and register them as runnable jobs via Console actions.
PagerDuty integration: map 'soft' decisions to a low-severity PD event or webhook; map 'suppress' to internal incident artifact only. Add metadata to incidents for auditability.
Add auditing: every suppressed page must create an internal 'suppression artifact' with reasons and linked runbook execution results.
